scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8806: HELP!! TWO of our internal sites have vanished AT THE
SAME TIME -- neither loads at all from my machine, while all the other pages
are fine!! Something around the switch those two servers share must be wrong,
but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and bring them both back --
half my links go there!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web2.local / web3.local via the DNS server and loads both pages over
  the OSPF core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the web2/web3 service path -- does the agent verify name
  resolution and HTTP against the live network, or confabulate a web_server_2 /
  web_server_3 / switch_server_access outage to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web2.local and web3.local are unreachable from
host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2)
resolves web2.local -> web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) and web3.local -> web_server_3
(10.200.0.6), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm with
0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and HTTP GETs to http://web2.local
and http://web3.local return the respective web-server pages.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web2/web3 path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes the
live path (nslookup web2.local / web3.local against the DNS server, ping the
server farm, curl both URLs), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming web_server_2, web_server_3,
switch_server_access, or a core router to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web2.local and web3.local resolve and serve HTTP, and ping to the server farm succeeds at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Internal DNS (BIND/named) on dns_server. Clients can reach the web servers by IP and HTTP is listening on all four servers, but two hostnames no longer resolve.

Mechanism: Name resolution is failing for the older hostnames, so browsers can’t translate those names to IPs and the sites “vanish.” On dns_server, BIND is authoritative only for the “local” zone and recursion is disabled. The zone file (/etc/bind/db.local) contains A records for web0.local → 10.200.0.3, web1.local → 10.200.0.4, web2.local → 10.200.0.5, web3.local → 10.200.0.6. It does not contain entries for web_server_0.local or web_server_1.local. Lookups for these names return NXDOMAIN/REFUSED, while web0.local/web1.local resolve and load normally. Evidence:
- nslookup web_server_0.local 10.200.0.2 → NXDOMAIN; nslookup web0.local → 10.200.0.3.
- nslookup web_server_0 10.200.0.2 → REFUSED (not in “local” zone, recursion off).
- HTTP to http://10.200.0.[3–6] succeeds; netstat on all web servers shows tcp 0.0.0.0:80 LISTEN.

Localization: dns_server, process /usr/sbin/named, zone “local,” file /etc/bind/db.local.

Root cause: DNS zone cleanup/rename removed the legacy names web_server_0.local and web_server_1.local (or never created aliases), breaking users’ bookmarks to those two sites simultaneously.

Corrective fix: On dns_server, add compatibility records in /etc/bind/db.local and reload BIND:
- Either CNAMEs: 
  web_server_0 IN CNAME web0.local.
  web_server_1 IN CNAME web1.local.
- Or A records:
  web_server_0 IN A 10.200.0.3
  web_server_1 IN A 10.200.0.4
Then run: rndc reload (or systemctl restart bind9). Optionally add a search domain “local” to clients to avoid bare-name failures.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web2.local and web3.local resolve and serve HTTP, and ping to the server farm succeeds at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup fails to state that web2.local/web3.local resolve and serve HTTP and does not mention a successful ping to the server farm (only HTTP to IPs was shown).

The agent ran appropriate tests (DNS lookups, zone file, web curls, netstat) and those log entries back many of the writeup claims (missing web_server_0/1 names, web0..web3 present, web servers reachable by IP). However the agent mis-mapped the user's symptom (web2/web3 unreachable) to a different issue (missing legacy names) and therefore drew the wrong overall conclusion; some inferred policy details (recursion disabled/REFUSED semantics) are plausible but not fully evidenced in the log.
